about: The front page as the editor wants it: what leads, what sits under it, what is service, the beats and the order of the bands. Kept by correspondent@PrompTugal.dinis and rewritten at each run, up to the last minute of the summit. Not yet read by the build: until dev@ wires newsroom/build/features/front.mjs to it (the ask in board/team/correspondent/status.json), the lead is simply the newest article, and when several share a date the order is an accident of file names. Articles are named by their slug in content/articles/.
edition: the Web Summit edition, 9 to 12 November 2026

lead.why: New at 08:26 (S13): EY's report, released at Web Summit's press conference on 5 November, puts ten Lisbon editions at almost 2.5 billion euros for Portugal's economy, set against what an earlier government study found. The biggest news on the site, national, and about Portugal: it leads. S9 takes the lead back when its round 2 (BR7: 236 Brazil-based startups on Web Summit's own list) lands.

Hard news on the mandate: three Portuguese funding rounds in a fortnight.
Lisbon's award winners with AI through several, and the Algarve's plan beyond tourism.

days.about: The front page by day, as Dinis asked at about 04:30 UTC on 6 November (board/guidance/2026-11-06-front-page-timeline-publication.md, section 2): a block of the days from Friday 6 to Friday 13 November, today highlighted; a past day shows the front page as it was then, a coming day what is planned for it (the talks, what to know). My editorial plan for each day; the counts of agenda items are from data/events/ at v0.1.113. dev@ builds the block, designer@ its look.

decisions_on_findings.what: C's 30-second briefing is the readers' favourite but its lines carry no source or author, and 'Play the briefing' does not say what it plays
decisions_on_findings.decision: accept: each briefing line is the headline of a published article and links it (so each carries that article's sources and byline); a line with no article behind it is not in the briefing. The words of the lines come from front-page.json's lead and top; the layout and the play button are designer@'s and dev@'s.

decisions_on_findings.what: 'Registration: collect your lanyard and wristband' three times under one title on the front page
decisions_on_findings.decision: accept: the place belongs in the title (Airport T1, Pavilhão de Portugal) or the three should show as one item with its places. The titles come from the programme desk's agenda and the derivation: for ontologist@ (or the programme desk), and dev@ if the front page should group them.
